text: Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures - Goo Gone Original adhesive remover (manufacturer SDS rev. 9/19/2024 + ingredient disclosure PDF), Shout Advanced Stain Remover Action Gel (SC Johnson SmartLabel + SDS 350000035250), The Works Toilet Bowl Cleaner (CA Cleaning Products Right to Know disclosure 12/27/2019 + manufacturer SDS + EPA label 5185-505-80306), and Bounce Fabric Softener Sheets Outdoor Fresh (P&G SmartLabel). 17 new ingredients. Grading: 4 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L with consensus denominators cited - Orange Oil (CID 62161, dominant block 10 notifications/262 reports: H315 90.5%, H317 90.5% -> derm D + allerg, H318 44.7% -> derm D, H411 90.1% -> env D; H226 at 39.7% below threshold, not graded); Methenamine (CID 4101, dominant block 19 notifications/1051 reports: H317 100% -> derm C + allerg); Undeceth-3 (CID 61930, two single-company notifications: H318 100% -> derm D, flagged Low confidence); Nonoxynol (CID 24773, 2 notifications/3 reports: H315 100% -> derm C, H412 100% -> env C, flagged Low confidence). 5 recorded Not Classified on a stated consensus - Solvent Orange 60 (2229/2274), CI Acid Blue 145 (5/5), Tripropylene Glycol Butyl Ether (no GHS section in PubChem), Diethylene Glycol (H302 100% of 38 notifications; acute oral is not a graded dimension), and 8 recorded unclassified with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/petroleum streams, minerals, materials or withheld trade-secret names with no PubChem CID (Petroleum Distillates Hydrotreated Light, Aliphatic Ether Alcohol, Glycol Ether, Polyester Sheet, Dialkylester Dimethyl Ammonium Methosulfate, Fatty Acids C16-18, Bentonite, Ethoxylated C8-18 Alkylamines, Turpentine) - never an invented grade. METHOD FINDING (recorded, not silently worked around): PubChem PUG View returns GHS classifications grouped by ECHA C&L notification group, and each group carries its own denominator. tools/grade_batch.py flattens all groups into one h_statements list, so a >=40% figure from a 2-notification fringe group is indistinguishable from a 19-notification consensus. Methenamine is the live example: its dominant group (19 notifications) carries H228+H317, while a separate 2-notification group carries H302/H314/H334/H351 at '100%' - within-group, not global. Those fringe codes were NOT graded. Grades in this run were taken from the dominant group with the denominator stated in each note. Regulatory: added a Nonoxynol entry (EU REACH Annex XVII entry 46 restricts NP/NPE at >=0.1% in domestic cleaning; US has no consumer-cleaner restriction) - The Works Toilet Bowl Cleaner discloses nonoxynol on a mainstream US product, which is the EU/US gap this section exists to show. Check attempted and REJECTED: Diethylene Glycol is not asserted as an EU harmonised Repr. 1B - the search result that suggested it was mixing in the borate row (same H360FD / 5.5% SCL), and the manufacturer SDSs found say DEG is not classified for reproductive or repeated-exposure toxicity. No reg entry filed.

Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures - Purex Free & Clear Liquid Laundry Detergent (Henkel/Purex public disclosure), Spray 'n Wash Laundry Stain Remover (Reckitt rbnainfo.com SmartLabel + SDS), Ivory Concentrated Dishwashing Liquid Classic Scent (P&G SmartLabel), fantastik Disinfectant Multi-Purpose Cleaner Fresh Scent (SC Johnson 'What's Inside'). 7 new ingredients: calcium chloride, potassium chloride, diisopropanolamine, sodium polyacrylate, fluorescent brightener 28, protease enzyme, PEI-14 PEG-24/PPG-16 copolymer. 3 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py with consensus percentages cited (calcium chloride H319 99.7% -> derm C; diisopropanolamine H318 51.2% -> derm D; fluorescent brightener 28 268/274 not-classified); 1 not-classified on consensus (potassium chloride 825/875); 3 recorded unclassified/extrapolated with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/polymers or generic class terms with no PubChem CID (sodium polyacrylate, PEI-14 copolymer, protease enzyme) - never an invented grade. Headline findings: (1) Spray 'n Wash discloses sodium tetraborate decahydrate (borax) as a sequestering agent - the same substance EU CLP classifies Reproductive toxicant 1B (H360FD) and restricts for consumer supply, still routine in a mainstream US stain remover. (2) Purex Free & Clear, marketed for sensitive skin as dye- and perfume-free, still contains methylisothiazolinone (a potent contact allergen) and sodium laureth sulfate. (3) fantastik's fragrance disclosure includes butylphenyl methylpropional (Lilial), an EU-banned CMR fragrance, plus hexyl cinnamal. 149 products, 219 ingredients.

Sifter lane: verified 9 graded ingredients against PubChem GHS (8 consistent, repo codes subsets of notifier aggregates); corrected Sodium Percarbonate H271→H272 (46.1% notifier consensus, oxidizer cat 2 not 1). Graded 5 fully-covered products via scorer methodology: Bar Keepers Friend D, Cascade D, Finish D, 20 Mule Team Borax F (H360FD), Organic Essential Oils Kit F. 145 products, 69 graded / 76 ungraded. No duplicates; validator green.

Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures — Persil ProClean Liquid Laundry Detergent Intense Fresh (Henkel SmartLabel, verified 16-Jan-2025), Clorox Clean-Up All Purpose Cleaner with Bleach Original (Clorox SmartLabel updated 11/19/2024 + SDS EPA Reg. 5813-21), Spic and Span All-Purpose Disinfecting Spray and Glass Cleaner (Church & Dwight SDS + retail disclosure), Downy Ultra Free & Gentle Liquid Fabric Conditioner (P&G SmartLabel updated 2024-11-04). 20 new ingredients. 13 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py, each with its consensus percentages cited and any sub-40% codes noted: laureth-12, sodium metaborate, tetrasodium iminodisuccinate, disodium distyrylbiphenyl disulfonate, myristamine oxide, sodium chlorate, benzophenone, sodium orthosilicate, isopropanolamine, tartaric acid, formic acid, pentasodium pentetate, cellulase enzyme. 7 recorded unclassified/extrapolated with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/polymers with no PubChem CID (fatty acid sodium soaps, polyethyleneimine alkoxylate, the acrylate/styrene copolymer, the polyoxyalkylene chromophore, mannanase enzyme, DEEDMAC, polyquaternium-33) — never an invented grade. Headline findings: (1) benzophenone, prohibited in EU cosmetics (Annex II, Entry 1703) and IARC 2B, is disclosed on the US label of a mainstream bleach spray cleaner — added as a reclassified entry plus a new reg entry (EU banned / US flagged). (2) sodium metaborate, the borate enzyme stabilizer in Persil, carries the same EU CLP Reproductive toxicant 1B (H360FD) classification as borax — added as a reclassified entry plus a reg entry (EU restricted / US allowed). (3) sodium chlorate on the Clorox Clean-Up label is not an added ingredient — it forms as the hypochlorite decays in storage (3 NaOCl -> NaClO3 + 2 NaCl), documented in the OxyChem hypochlorite handbook. (4) Downy Free & Gentle is marketed perfume-free yet still discloses a 'Fragrance Ingredient'. Verification note: the PubChem name lookup for 'Protease' silently returned Bacillomycin (CID 3086051) — a different compound — so it was discarded and the disclosure recorded under the existing 'Subtilisin' entry instead. Validator: pending. Products 141 -> 145, ingredient keys 192 -> 212.

Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures — Clorox Disinfecting Wipes Fresh Scent (Clorox SmartLabel, updated 4/8/2025), OxiClean Versatile Stain Remover (Church & Dwight SDS), Woolite Delicates Laundry Detergent (Reckitt SmartLabel), Mr. Clean Magic Eraser (P&G SDS composition section). 15 new ingredients. 7 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py (hexoxyethanol, triethanolamine, BHT, butylphenyl methylpropional, hexyl salicylate, isoeugenol, eugenol), each with its consensus percentages cited and any sub-40% codes noted. 8 recorded unclassified/extrapolated with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/polymers with no PubChem CID (sodium polycarboxylate, the melamine-formaldehyde copolymer, the two BAC-type quats, TEA cocoate, C10-16 pareth, C12-14 alcohols ethoxylated propoxylated, sodium C10-16 alkylbenzenesulfonate) — never an invented grade. Headline finding: butylphenyl methylpropional (Lilial), a CMR 1B fragrance banned in EU cosmetics since 2022, is still disclosed in a US detergent — added as a reclassified entry plus a new reg entry (EU banned / US allowed) noting the SCCS record that the cosmetics ban does not reach household cleaners. Validator: 0 issues. 141 products, 192 ingredients.

Root-cause fix for the duplicate bug that had been hand-fixed five times: the grow lane's dedupe index was keyed raw (.strip().lower()) while its lookup used norm() (punctuation collapsed), so every seed product whose name or brand contains punctuation (P&G, Free & Clear, Multi-Surface) silently re-added itself each run — which is exactly why Clorox Disinfecting Bleach, the one seed with no punctuation, never duplicated. Index normalized in bulk_ingest.py and a permanent `chem_maintain.py --dedupe --fix` guard wired into chem_cron.sh, so duplicates can no longer survive a run. Removed 4 duplicates (137->133). Schema fixes: 3 invalid enum values closed — Bac-Out impact 'sens'->'allerg', and the non-canonical grade dim 'allerg' on Linalool/Geraniol merged into derm:D per the house H317 rule (matching Citral/Limonene/Fragrance). Gather: 4 popular US products with public disclosures — Resolve Heavy Traffic Foam Carpet Cleaner (Reckitt SmartLabel), Krud Kutter Original Cleaner & Degreaser (Rust-Oleum SDS), Weiman Stainless Steel Cleaner & Polish (Weiman ingredient list), LA's Totally Awesome All-Purpose Cleaner (manufacturer MSDS + retail composition — flagged as weaker sourcing, not presented as equivalent). 12 new ingredients, each graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py where a CID exists, or recorded unclassified with an explicit note where it does not (UVCB/polymer) rather than guessing a grade. Added CMIT regulatory entry: EU leave-on cosmetics ban since 2016, no equivalent US federal restriction in cleaning products. Validator: 0 issues. 137 products, 177 ingredients.
